subject: KV-cache separation & mesh-adapter proposal for FinWorks private VPC
messages:
From: Ahaan Mehta <amaan@finworks.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: KV-cache separation & mesh-adapter idea (kickoff)

Thanks for taking the time earlier today. Per our call, FinWorks is worried about the KV cache residency on the inference nodes mixing with tenant network paths — we'd like an architecture that keeps customer KV/contexts strictly inside the data-plane hostgroup while allowing the control plane (updates, model management) to use a separate mesh adapter that can egress to our audit collectors.

High level asks:
- KV cache pinned to local fast storage on tenant runtime nodes with explicit egress rules (no public egress)
- Control plane communicates via a mesh-adapter (L7) that sits in a small DMZ and routes management calls to the control plane endpoints
- We need a reference diagram and short ops playbook (start/stop failure modes)

Can Redwood share a reference diagram + a short decision writeup we can include in our security review?

Thanks,
Ahaan
Senior Network Architect, FinWorks

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Ahaan Mehta <amaan@finworks.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KV-cache separation & mesh-adapter idea (kickoff)

Ahaan — thanks, this is exactly the right framing. Attaching a first-pass diagram (kv-sep-diagram_v2.png) and a short proposal (mesh-adapter-proposal.pdf). Quick notes inline: 

- We recommend logical split: runtime nodes (data-plane) own the KV store and only accept inference calls from the tenant network. Control plane calls (model rollouts, health probes) go through the mesh-adapter which is a colocated L7 proxy in the control-subnet.
- Mesh-adapter functions: TLS termination to control plane, authz auditing to your collector via an outbound-only egress ACL, and rate limiting to protect control-plane endpoints.
- KV-residency: use an encrypted local volume (LUKS) with KMS integration; do not mount KV volumes on control-plane hosts.

Irene and Karthik — can you validate the failure modes and add a short ops playbook (start/stop, how we fail open vs fail closed for control-plane loss)?

Deliverables in folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cKVcacheProposal
Attachments: kv-sep-diagram_v2.png (PNG, 1.2MB), mesh-adapter-proposal.pdf (PDF, 680KB)

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Ahaan Mehta <amaan@finworks.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KV-cache separation & mesh-adapter idea (kickoff)

Looping in my notes after walking the diagram: 

- Failure modes:
  * Control-plane unavailable but data-plane up: inference continues from local KV; model rollout is delayed. Recommend a canary-based rollout gating and a TTL-based KV invalidation to avoid stale context.
  * Data-plane node isolation (network partition): node continues serving cached contexts but should be marked as READ-ONLY in the roster to avoid writes to the global store.
  * Mesh-adapter failure: must be recoverable via a second adapter in another AZ with automated DNS failover.

- Operational playbook (short):
  1) Mesh-adapter restart: drain control-plane flows (graceful 30s), restart adapter, validate auth logs shipped to FinWorks collector.
  2) KV corruption detection: health check detects corrupted LSM segment; automates an offline repair job, mark node as quarantined and shift traffic.
  3) Emergency rollback: pin runtime to previous model artifact via control-plane API (read-only control path available via emergency key).

I've added the runbook snippets into the shared PDF (mesh-adapter-proposal.pdf, section 3). Karthik — any changes on the egress ACL / service routing notes?

-Irene
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, Ahaan Mehta <amaan@finworks.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: KV-cache separation & mesh-adapter idea (kickoff)

Thanks all — quick routing/ACL notes from infra: 

- Egress: mesh-adapter uses a single NATed outbound IP range that is allowlisted by FinWorks; control-plane endpoints are authenticated via mTLS using certs issued by FinWorks' CA (we'll accept their CA or integrate with their KMS).
- VLAN/Segmentation: runtime nodes should be on a tenant-segmented VPC with host-based firewall rules that only allow 9000/tcp for inference and 22/ssh from the ops jumpbox. No direct outbound 443 from runtime nodes — only the mesh-adapter has outbound 443 for control messages.
- Observability: adapter will emit structured JSON traces to your collector; we will also ship a periodic inventory snapshot (node UUID, KV index size, last-sync) to a read-only S3 bucket you control for audits.

Next steps: 
1) FinWorks to confirm allowlist IPs and CA details.
2) Redwood to produce a short cutover checklist for staging -> prod (we'll include a staged DNS failover and canary model window).

I'll incorporate these into INF-7842.

Karthik Iyer
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
